title: Regional degradation probing and backpressure safety harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a controlled fault-injection harness that probes progressive regional degradation and GPU-pool backpressure while enforcing automatic circuit breakers and safe rollback. The goal is to validate SLO preservation and graceful degraded-mode behavior for multi-region traffic routing, eviction policies, and dependency failovers without exposing production customers to large-scale errors. This ticket covers design, implementation of non-invasive probes, telemetry collection, and an initial canary run in staging followed by a monitored limited-production window.
scenarios: 1) Gradual region egress: inject increasing packet loss and API latency on region-eu until we observe routing and evacuation policies trigger within configured SLO thresholds.
2) GPU pool exhaustion: create synthetic workload to fill a dedicated GPU pool to capacity and measure autoscaler behavior, queueing latencies, and request shedding impact on pinned tenants.
3) Dependency blackhole shim: route Redis/kv and S3 calls for a test tenant to a blackhole shim that returns timeouts; validate fallback caches, circuit breakers, and error budgets.
4) Combined pressure: run GPU pool exhaustion in region-us-west while inducing a degraded dependency in region-us-east to validate cross-region fallback and cost-aware routing decisions.
5) Canary throttles: apply rate-limited shedding on 1% of traffic in production to validate observability and rollback automation before scaling to larger percentages.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can reproducibly create the five scenarios in staging and collect full telemetry without manual intervention.
SLO violations are bounded and mapped to clear rollback thresholds: if error budget > 5% in 15m then abort and heal.
Circuit breaker behavior validated: downstream calls tripped within configured timeout windows and recovered cleanly once dependency restored.
Failover routing moved >95% of traffic to healthy regions within the target RTO in at least three independent runs.
Runbook produced with step-by-step rollback, emergency stop, and post-mortem template.
harness_components: Non-invasive network fault injector (controlled packet loss/latency) with region-scoped targets.
Synthetic GPU workload generator that can simulate KV-cache heavy and generation-heavy request mixes.
Dependency blackhole shim service with deterministic timeout/response behaviors and request tagging for observability.
Traffic tagging and small-percentage canary routing via control-plane flags to avoid wide blast radius.
Telemetry sink and dashboard template (latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, token throughput, queue depth, GPU utilization, evictions).
Automated gate that triggers rollback when configured SLO thresholds or safety limits are exceeded.
metrics: Error rate (5xx) and classified errors by cause (GPU-queue-drop, dependency-timeout, routing-fallback)
Token-generation throughput per region and per model variant
GPU pool utilization and queue depth
Time-to-failover (RTO) and failback (RPO) when region becomes healthy
Number of circuit-breaker trips and average blackout duration
Observed cost delta during test (estimated incremental $)
safety_controls: Start in isolated staging environment with full telemetry retention for 30d.
Canary percentage limited to 1% traffic in production initial window with manual approval required for >1%.
Automatic abort if customer-facing p95 increases by >40% or error rate increases >3% absolute within 10 minutes.
Control-plane manual kill switch and automated healthwatcher that resumes normal routing after remediation.
No targeting of high-SLA enterprise tenants; test tenants flagged and excluded from billing impact.
test_plan: Week 1: implement harness components and unit tests; internal code review and security scan.
Week 2: run scenarios 1-3 in staging with 10 independent runs each; collect telemetry and tune thresholds.
Week 3: perform combined pressure scenario in staging; generate runbook and post-test analysis.
Week 4: schedule limited production canary (1% traffic) during low-traffic window; on-call and SRE present; run for 2 hours.
Post-canarY: full post-mortem, update console dashboards, and propose automation for recurring smoke checks if results are clean.
